name: Short before the London fixes

why: +0.216 R/trade over 20 trades, PF 2.113, passes every screen

source: Donati & Jung 2019 (same thesis); context: Caminschi & Heaney, Journal of Futures Markets 2014
original_rules: Short 05:05-05:35 and 09:35-10:05 New York time (around the AM and PM London fixes). No stops.
implementation: As stated, in New York time.
deviations: London and New York change clocks on different dates; the thesis's New York times were kept.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

execution.costs: frozen Phase 5 cost model: candle spread (0.30 fallback), commission 3.50 USD/lot/side, slippage 0.05 USD per fill
execution.r_unit: The source has no stop: R is a NOMINAL unit of 1.5 x ATR(14) on M15 at entry (GoldScalp's default ATR stop size). Marked nominal; USD results are always reported too.

range.note: The same 14 calendar days (10 trading days) as stage 1. Classification uses this window only.

Supplementary, about 11 weeks of the same spent development series. Once-a-day rules cannot reach 15 trades in 10 trading days; this run shows more trades for them. It does not classify anything and is not validation.

evidence_at_registration.note: Both windows are development data. The context window contains the screen days.

assessment: The most consistent result of the screen. It passed the 10-day screen, held over the 11-week context run in both its morning and afternoon windows, and its two half hours ranked 1st and 2nd of 46 in a placebo test. A longer run over 2026, made after registration, was much weaker: it lost money in January to June.
caveats: Short-only, and gold fell about 11 % over the 11 weeks.
Not stable across 2026: over 1 January to 13 November (420 trades) it made +0.063 nominal R per trade, but lost $168 over 224 trades in January to June and made $774 over 196 trades from July.
Most of the 2026 result is the morning fix; the afternoon fix is about break-even once costs are doubled.
Almost flat in August, when the market was flat (+$14 over 22 trades).
The source reports the effect in some years only.
No stop in the source: the risk per trade is undefined, and R is a nominal unit.
next_questions: Does it survive a rising market (for example January-May 2026, already-used data)?
What stop gives a defined risk without changing the idea?
restrictions: Screening only: not validated, not shown to be profitable, not trading-ready.
Its Strategy Lab form (LAB_STRATEGIES.json) was added on 16 November 2026 at the owner's request. Live or demo results of that form are not a validation of this candidate.
The rules are frozen as screened. A changed rule is a new candidate with a new id.
Development data already used for it: all 2026 history before the forward boundary (1 January to 29 May and 22 June to 13 November 2026). None of it is validation data.
Any validation must use data research has not touched (forward data from 14 November 2026) under a registered, frozen protocol.
